claim_summary: For every finite d, analytic full-support uniformly strongly log-concave experiments with identical tangent Fisher matrix diag(a^2 exp(-2i)/3) have different one-sample archive orders as epsilon shrinks: the product experiment requires Omega(log^2(1/epsilon)) bits, while a full-dimensional thin-noise correlated experiment has a positive blind classical codec using at most (1/(3 ln 2)) log^1.5(1/epsilon)+O(log(1/epsilon)) bits.
scope: Dimension d may grow with precision. The correlated score law is absolutely continuous in each finite dimension but is not bounded below on a fixed full score cube; result addresses covariance-only dimension-uniform archive estimates, not conditional thickness theorems.
costs_and_limits: Memory counts one combined input-dependent label; exact transforms, random-bit generation, arithmetic, model acquisition, and finite-precision simulation are outside the idealized memory-only interface.
The archive upper is a mathematical positive Markov codec, not a finite-bit implementation.
Numerical checks are finite diagnostics, not proof certification or novelty evidence.
Cross-phase overlap with c09_s02, c09_l03, and c09_l05 is attributed in R1.txt; the R2 thin-noise extension has no independent literature/priority clearance.
